author: WP17
summary: Quick-reference appendix mapping input, audio/media, devices, networking/gamer services, storage and sharp-runtime core types to their boundaries, plus language bindings and showcase applications. Service rows are already covered in depth by the services and sharp-runtime deep dives; stale numbers (five storage tests, 16,201/2,183 database rows, six bindings, ABI 0.20 windows, early cna-studio, no GPU run for the car simulator) were corrected. A new reference page carries the map, the binding rule and the pinned application table.

concepts.text: A companion map groups the framework-service and sharp-runtime surface by stable API role and puts the current implementation boundary beside each; exact signatures belong to the headers and delivery, ownership and evidence to the owner pages.

concepts.section: Input: Keyboard, Mouse, GamePad, and Touch
concepts.text: Keyboard exposes snapshot state plus marked scancode, modifier and naming helpers; an XNA Keys value, a physical scancode and a layout name must not be collapsed.

concepts.section: Input: Keyboard, Mouse, GamePad, and Touch
concepts.text: Mouse positions are in the renderer's logical coordinates; logical presentation, window, physical-pixel and post-present coordinates diverge by renderer and host.
tokens: Logical coordinates are a renderer contract

concepts.section: Input: Keyboard, Mouse, GamePad, and Touch
concepts.text: GamePad is player-indexed with dead-zone modes and vibration plus EXT identity, light-bar, trigger-rumble and sensor readers; device opening, hot-plug and mapping have separate evidence.

concepts.section: Input: Keyboard, Mouse, GamePad, and Touch
concepts.text: TouchPanel gives a per-update snapshot, display metadata and gesture dequeue; a desktop run without a touch device exercises the API, not physical touch, and web and mobile paths differ.

concepts.section: Input: Keyboard, Mouse, GamePad, and Touch
concepts.text: CNA::Input adds clipboard, raw joystick, haptics, sensor, power and device-enumeration services outside XNA's surface, with platform-specific absence or refusal.

concepts.section: Input: Keyboard, Mouse, GamePad, and Touch
concepts.text: A state object constructible without hardware is not evidence that a host delivered the event or that the renderer maps coordinates back into the same logical space.
tokens: is not evidence that a host delivered the event

target.evidence: modules/input (state types are plain value snapshots)

concepts.text: SoundEffect's 3D model is CNA's own approximation over its mixer, which depends on the audio implementation (SDL3_mixer for SDL3, CNA's own mixer for ALSA, none for SDL2/NULL); instance disposal and ownership are observable contracts.
concepts.note: The unit says the approximation is over SDL3_mixer; that holds for the SDL3 audio implementation only.

concepts.text: DynamicSoundEffectInstance streams 16-bit PCM and, as a CNAEXT, float buffers; the two modes cannot be mixed while playing, and queue timing and callback thread need runtime evidence.
XACT wave banks, sound banks, cues, categories, variables and runtime parameter control are parsed and played in a substantial subset by CNA's own engine, with unsupported fields explicit.
Song and MediaPlayer ownership, callback order and metadata differ between files, libraries and active playback, and no Song route accepts MIDI even though the vendored mixer can decode it.
Video decoding needs the optional FFmpeg backend; decoded frame, uploaded texture and synchronised playback are distinct milestones, and without the backend playback throws NotSupportedException.
A reader accepting a file does not prove that a mixer or video device played it, nor that its events arrived on the intended thread.
tokens: A reader accepting a file does not prove

concepts.text: Sensors expose support, state, interval, current value and change events; the platform service covers only part of the vocabulary, readings arrive off the game thread, web targets are refused, and synthetic injection is not physical delivery.

VibrateController stores a request that is not proof of motor engagement; emulator and physical hardware are different evidence tiers; CNAEXT adds intensity, left/right motors, support and device name.

CNA::Devices (camera, display and system information, dialogs, URL launch, locale, clipboard, tray, power) sits behind an opt-in option and many services report unavailable on headless or unsupported hosts.
NetworkSession's local discovery and ENet delivery are real only for SystemLink; it is not Xbox LIVE matchmaking and gives no Internet traversal.
Packet framing, peer identity, ordering and leave/disconnect transitions of LocalNetworkGamer/NetworkGamer need two-process hostile-input tests.
SignedInGamer and related types are local substitutes that keep the API shape without claiming Xbox LIVE service equivalence.
AvatarRenderer keeps the faithful base avatar API while SkinnedModelEXT is a separate opt-in real-rendering route; neither supplies Microsoft's avatar service or assets.
StorageDevice is fake-async and a local-filesystem substitute for platform UI; its focused suite is 14 GoogleTest definitions in StorageDeviceTests.cpp, not five.
concepts.note: The unit says five focused tests.

concepts.text: StorageContainer operations go through a shared containment helper that rejects traversal and symlink escape with focused tests, while the glob-pattern queries have no direct pattern tests.
Evidence from one storage operation must not be transferred to all storage behaviour.
tokens: Do not transfer evidence from one storage operation

concepts.text: System::Object and type helpers give .NET-shaped naming, equality, hash and string over standard C++ objects and RTTI, with no CLR object header, reflection universe, universal boxing or garbage collector.
Primitive aliases and String map C# vocabulary onto fixed-width C++ types and UTF-8 storage; managed-string semantics need explicit per-operation work.
tokens: String is an API vocabulary, not storage

concepts.text: TimeSpan and date/time types are tick-based value types with explicit arithmetic and validation; time-zone breadth is bounded.
EventHandler<T> combines the C# delegate and event roles with subscription, removal, clearing and snapshot raise; lifetime and thread safety remain contracts.
tokens: EventHandler: the event keyword C++ does not have

concepts.text: Collections and task/thread primitives are translation-friendly subsets whose APIs may be implemented, ignored or out of scope.
tokens: Tasks: a real but scoped async model

concepts.text: Stream, MemoryStream and readers/writers provide byte I/O whose ownership, closed-state behaviour, encodings and exception types must be checked per implementation.
tokens: Closing closes operations, not the bytes

concepts.text: The sharp-runtime planning database is a set of workflow classifications, not a completion score: 16,207 task rows and 2,417 ticket rows at 41b918c9 (earlier totals belong to earlier revisions).
concepts.note: The unit quotes 16,201 task rows and 2,183 tickets for an older pin.

concepts.section: Language bindings: projected surfaces over a moving ABI
concepts.text: The binding projects are independent deliverables, not proof supplied by the C++ repository; eight are public (C#, Java, TypeScript, Python, Rust, Swift, and since 2026-09-25 Go and Ruby).

concepts.section: Language bindings: projected surfaces over a moving ABI
concepts.text: Each binding's admission window in code is the 0.21 ABI generation (Ruby also 0.7.0); READMEs that still say 0.20 are stale, and status words differ per binding (C# 'not yet behaviorally complete or release-ready', Python 'pre-alpha').
tokens: several READMEs still say 0.20.0 where the code says 0.21
not yet behaviorally complete or release-ready
concepts.note: The unit gives C#, Java and TypeScript ABI 0.20 from their READMEs. Per-binding host-execution details (Java HEADLESS/NULL, Python wheel) were not re-checked.

concepts.section: Language bindings: projected surfaces over a moving ABI
concepts.text: CNA 009d40f5 exports ABI 0.29.0; a structurally complete language surface is not binary compatibility, so a binding release must regenerate or audit declarations, admit the new version explicitly, rebuild its adapter and rerun its host matrix.

concepts.section: Language bindings: projected surfaces over a moving ABI
concepts.text: The C ABI is a foundation for bindings, not an automatic compatibility certificate.
tokens: Compatibility is not established by this source revision

concepts.text: cna-car-simulator is a passenger-car simulator with deterministic headless captures; at 04e4d104 its README also records eight deterministic scenes measured on an AMD Radeon 780M, so 'no real-GPU run recorded' is stale.
concepts.note: The unit says no real-GPU run had been recorded at its pin.

concepts.text: cna-city is a 100,000-agent technology demonstration that stresses CNAEXT shadows, HDR, post-processing, instancing and culling and publishes the engine boundaries it meets.

cna-street is a scene and asset-pipeline case study (photogrammetry and CC0/CC-BY assets with recorded licences, glTF PBR, audio); its tests at 506cef1f are fourteen CPU-only suites and its lock pins CNA d4220380, easy-gl deda7a42 and meta-gl 20c8b2dc.
concepts.note: The unit mentions screenshot regression; the README at this pin describes CPU-only suites.

concepts.text: cna-studio is a separate authoring tool that produces ordinary CNA projects, is not a CNA runtime dependency and is not CNA's Inspector; at 1.0.0 (2026-09-23) it entered maintenance mode rather than being early.
living-room-simulator is a completed nine-milestone simulation with its own CPU-only tests and documented limitations, not a framework conformance suite.
These applications' screenshots, tests and claims belong to their own pins and do not upgrade CNA 009d40f5's renderer, platform or API evidence.
tokens: They do not upgrade the renderer, platform or API evidence

concepts.text: Take exact declarations from CNA's module-owned headers and sharp-runtime's headers at the revision used, then require the matching evidence tier.
A type name shared by XNA, FNA, CNA and sharp-runtime establishes lineage, not identical ownership, exceptions, threading, encoding, platform reach or behaviour.
